388	## Recommendation for Kent — best first
389	
390	### 1. Recommended: name the Hormuz contract, and keep the Brent ending honest about having none
391	
392	Two edits to the fixture, and the demo gains a clickable venue price **and**
393	keeps the "no contract" path on screen — both halves of the story on one map.
394	
395	**(a) Rewrite claim `H`'s resolution to the venue's own words**, so the
396	comparison is like with like:
397	
398	> criteria: "IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls
399	> ('Arrivals of Ships') for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any
400	> date up to 31 October 2026."
401	> source: "IMF PortWatch transit-call data for the Strait of Hormuz."
402	> by: 2026-11-01 (unchanged — it already agrees with the market)
403	
404	**(b) Add one `market` ending off `H`** — call it `M3` — with a
405	`ContractPayoff(venue="Polymarket", contract_id=<the condition id>,
406	title="Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by October 31?", side="yes")`,
407	and record its quote: **mid .07, bid .06, offer .08, read 2026-09-21 14:48 UTC.**
408	
409	**(c) Leave `M1` exactly where it is**, as the `no_contract` case, printing
410	*"no contract quotes this claim — edge not calculable"*. With no quote there is
411	no break-even in probability; the honest break-even for the Brent trade is a
412	**price** — *"this pays if front-month Brent settles below $68"* — and it needs
413	the FRED `DCOILBRENTEU` spot anchor the digest already plans (§2.4), not a
414	Polymarket number.
415	
416	**Cost:** the two fixture edits are small. The structural cost is real and worth
417	saying out loud: **`H` is the hypothesis, and on the branch it is supposed true**,
418	so `M3`'s edge must be computed from the **base** world or it is exactly the
419	A1 trap. The digest's `priced(base, shown, …)` signature already forces that.
420	**Buys:** a live, liquid, $755k contract, whose deadline matches to the day,
421	that a reader can open in a browser from the Inspector.
422	
423	**What the card will say, and it is worth reading twice:** the model's
424	unconditional number for `H` is its prior, **.35**; the venue says **.07**. That
425	is a 28-point disagreement, and it is the single most interesting sentence this
426	product can print — provided the tool is honest that most of the gap is the
427	*claim* being harder to satisfy than it looked, not alpha. Until (a) is done,
428	the right label is `NotComparable(reason="different_question")`.
429	
430	### 2. Alternative: add `M3` and touch nothing else
431	
432	Skip (a). The venue price is still real, clickable and recorded, and the card
433	prints `different_question` with both questions side by side. **Cheaper, and
434	arguably more honest** — it demonstrates the `NotComparable` path on a real
435	contract instead of a missing one. **Costs** the headline "the model says X, the
436	venue says Y" moment, which becomes "the venue asks a different question, here
437	is how".
438	
439	### 3. The fallback R11 names, if Kent wants no new claim at all
440	
441	Keep the stand-in, mark `M1`'s quote `source: "user"` and print *"no contract
442	quotes this claim — edge not calculable"* with a price break-even. **This is
443	what happens by default and it is defensible** — but it leaves a map on which
444	nothing is priced, on a venue that in fact prices four of its seven claims to
445	within a near miss.
446	
447	### 4. Regardless of 1–3: fix `N1`, and consider `S`
448	
449	`N1.not_tradeable_reason` — *"No venue quotes a contract on a diplomatic
450	round"* — is **false**, and cheaply falsified by anyone who looks. Either rewrite
451	`N1` as a `market` claim naming **"US x Iran diplomatic meeting by October 31,
452	2026?"** (.33/.35, $184k traded, and its rules explicitly admit *"Indirect
453	in-person diplomacy through designated mediators"*), or rewrite the reason to
454	the truth: *"the contracts that exist ask about any mediated US-Iran round, not
455	specifically an Omani-mediated one."* The branch's `S` has the same
456	opportunity in the NO side of **"US x Iran ceasefire continues through October
457	31?"** (.51/.52) — but that market is **US-initiated strikes only**, where `S`
458	would accept an Israeli one, so it is a near miss to be labelled, not adopted.
459	
460	---
461	
462	## What I did not check
463	
464	- **Polymarket's terms of use.** The page is client-rendered and I did not read
465	  the text. This is the one open question that bears directly on committing a
466	  dated quote file to a public repository.
467	- **The fee schedule** (`/trading/fees`). So the `costs` term in a break-even is
468	  half the spread only; taker fees, if any, are not in my numbers.
469	- **Any rate limit, by testing.** I made roughly twenty-five calls and stopped.
470	- **The website's own search interface in a browser.** I used
471	  `/public-search`, which is the endpoint the site itself calls, but I did not
472	  confirm that by watching the site.
473	- **Whether a Brent market ever existed and closed.** My unfiltered `q=brent`
474	  search returned ten events and all were people or Brentford; I did not page
475	  through all 159 results.
476	- **Kalshi**, which ADR-0010 names third and which is stronger on commodities —
477	  a Brent contract may well exist there. Not my brief; worth an hour.
478	- **The POST batch endpoints** (`/books`, `/midpoints`) that `make record-quotes`
479	  would actually want, and `data-api`'s `prices-history`. Documented, not called.
480	- **`/api-reference/geoblock`**, so I cannot confirm ADR-0010's claim about
481	  reads being ungeoblocked beyond the fact that all twenty-five of mine worked.
482	- **Whether an October WTI monthly event appears on 1 October.** The pattern
483	  suggests it will; the September one ends 2026-10-01 and no October event exists
484	  today. If Kent wants a *crude* contract rather than a *Hormuz* one, that is the
485	  thing to look at again in ten days — it would still be WTI, not Brent.

# The Polymarket look — does the Hormuz map name anything real?

**Agent P · 2026-09-21 · read-only · no key, no cookie, no money spent.**
Every number below was read from a live call whose raw response is saved under
`plans/analysis/scripts/polymarket-look/`, with the exact `curl` line in
`commands.sh` beside it. Quote times are UTC and given to the minute.

---

## The answer in three lines

1. **Nothing on Polymarket quotes Brent crude.** Not today, not in the search
   index at all: every hit for *brent* is a person's first name or Brentford
   Football Club. Polymarket's only crude contracts are on **WTI**, and only in
   daily, weekly and current-month "did it touch a level" form. So the map's
   `M1` ending, `brent-below-70-2026-10-31`, names nothing and can name nothing.
2. **But the map's *hypothesis* has a real, live, liquid contract.**
   *"Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by October 31?"* — **7¢ mid, 6/8
   bid-offer, $119k resting, $755k traded, settles 2026-11-01**, and its deadline
   is the same day as claim `H`'s. Different measuring instrument (IMF PortWatch
   transit calls, not Lloyd's List) and a much easier test, so it is a near miss
   on the words and an exact hit on the subject and the date.
3. **Therefore the card says two things at once, and that is the strongest
   version of the demo.** On the Brent ending: *"no contract quotes this claim —
   edge not calculable"*, with a break-even. On the hypothesis: a real venue
   price the reader can click, beside the model's own — *the model says 35%, the
   venue says 7%* — which is exactly the moment R11 was hoping for, moved one
   tile up the map.

**One correction that falls out and is not optional.** Claim `N1` says it cannot
be traded because *"No venue quotes a contract on a diplomatic round."* Polymarket
quotes three: **"US x Iran diplomatic meeting by October 31, 2026?"** at 33/35
with $184k traded, plus a September and a December version. That sentence is
false and a reader who checks will find it false in under a minute.

---

## The candidates

Read 2026-09-21, **14:48 UTC**. Prices are the YES outcome. "Fit" judges the
question, not the subject: same underlying, same threshold, same deadline, same
resolution source.

| Map claim | Polymarket market | Bid / Offer / Mid | Liquidity · Volume | Ends | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M1** *Brent below $70 on 2026-10-31* | — **nothing exists** | — | — | — | **No contract.** Polymarket has never listed Brent. |
| **H** *Strait reopens, 14 consecutive days* | **Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by October 31?** | .06 / .08 / **.07** | $119,187 · $754,974 | 2026-11-01 03:59Z | **Near miss — the best on the venue.** Same subject, deadline within a day. Different instrument (IMF PortWatch) and a far easier test. |
| **H**, shorter window | Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by September 30? | .005 / .006 / — | $283,172 · $9,188,399 | 2026-10-01 03:59Z | Same question, wrong window — expires the day the fixture is set on. |
| **H**, longer window | Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by November 30? | .11 / .12 / — | $58,666 · $390,695 | 2026-12-01 04:59Z | Same question, one month long. |
| **N1** *Omani-mediated US-Iran talks resume publicly* | **US x Iran diplomatic meeting by October 31, 2026?** | .33 / .35 / — | $14,816 · $183,862 | 2026-10-31 23:59Z | **Near miss, and it kills `not_tradeable_reason`.** Mediated indirect talks qualify explicitly; it does not require Oman. |
| **N1**, the Oman half | Iran-Oman Hormuz Agreement by October 31? | .32 / .34 / — | $13,347 · $182,837 | 2026-10-31 23:59Z | An *agreement*, not a *round of talks*. Adjacent, not the same question. |
| **S** *A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory* | **US x Iran ceasefire continues through October 31?** (NO side) | .51 / .52 / — | $115,831 · $295,819 | 2026-10-31 23:59Z | **Near miss.** Its NO side is "the US strikes Iran by Oct 31" — but US-initiated only, air or surface-to-surface only, so it misses an Israeli strike, which the branch's `S` would accept. |
| **B** *Brent settles below $68 for five sessions* | *Will WTI Crude Oil hit (LOW) $70 in September?* | .012 / .015 / — | part of a $6.9m event | 2026-10-01 04:00Z | **Not the same question on three counts:** WTI not Brent (a different benchmark, usually a few dollars cheaper), a touch at any point rather than five settlements, and September rather than to 15 October. |
| **M2** *XLE underperforms SPY by 3%* | — nothing. `q=XLE` returns **zero** events. | — | — | — | **No contract.** Equities are not a Polymarket asset class. |
| **R** *OPEC+ announces output restraint* | — nothing on output. The five OPEC hits are *"Will another country leave OPEC in 2026?"*, *"OPEC dissolves in 2026?"* and three Gulf-diplomacy markets. | — | — | — | **No contract.** |
| **C** *Lloyd's war-risk premium below 0.4%* | — nothing. Insurance is not quoted. | — | — | — | **No contract.** |

A useful aside the venue hands over for free: on 2026-09-21 the September WTI
event has *hit (LOW) $90* already resolved YES, *hit (LOW) $85* at .30 and *hit
(HIGH) $100* at .26. **WTI is somewhere near $88–100 right now, so Brent below
$68 or $70 by 31 October is far out of the money in the real world** — which is
consistent with the fixture's own story (a strait still disrupted), but a reader
who prices the fixture against today will notice.

---

## The best candidate, in full

**Title:** `Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by October 31?`
**Public URL:** https://polymarket.com/event/strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to-normal-by-october-31-20260810151043583
**Event id** `830253` · **Market id** `3501950`
**Condition id** `0x405b56fc75f56d7635a94df9836d6cb6f9b9571d1fd33eb165c1e59d1d11801f`
**Question id** `0x11dd567a1641ecc26d40d65d21d4558ed6c1659e3b6cde7fa9442e11b8431585`
**Outcome token ids** — `outcomes` is `["Yes","No"]`, index for index with
`clobTokenIds`:
- YES `65318042793305154928481822061228422214615698483328483747495637152414701080541`
- NO  `112428165813371561912833460698436648539922320261306010177252036814838759682453`

**State at 2026-09-21 14:48 UTC** — `active: true`, `closed: false`,
`acceptingOrders: true`, `restricted: true`, `enableOrderBook: true`.
Liquidity **$119,187.28**, volume **$754,974.31**, open interest **$398,671.88**,
24-hour volume **$5,061.18**. Tick size **0.01**, minimum order **5**.

**The quote, YES token, read 2026-09-21 14:48:28 UTC** (the order book's own
millisecond stamp, `1790002107921`):
best bid **0.06** (6,624.83 size) · best offer **0.08** (9,693.30) ·
midpoint **0.07** · spread **0.02** · last trade **0.08**.
Gamma's rounded display figure `outcomePrices` reads `["0.07","0.93"]`.

**End date:** `2026-11-01T03:59:00Z` — that is 23:59 New York time on 31 October.
Claim `H` in the fixture resolves by `2026-11-01`. **The deadlines agree.**

**The resolution rules, word for word** (from the market's `description`; its
`resolutionSource` field is an empty string — on every market I looked at, the
rules live in `description` and `resolutionSource` is unused):

> This market will resolve to "Yes" if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving
> average of transit calls ("Arrivals of Ships") for the Strait of Hormuz equal
> to or above 60 for any date between market creation and October 31, 2026.
> Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".
>
> Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general
> cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be
> considered.
>
> This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving
> average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data
> has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such
> value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of
> the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that
> period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.
>
> Revisions to previously published data points made within this market's
> timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously
> published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data
> points after data is published for October 31, 2026, however, will not be
> considered.
>
> In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market
> may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on
> which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity
> issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data,
> and do not include cases where IMF Portwatch differs from alternative sources.
>
> The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the
> transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at
> https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the
> chart and through downloadable files.

**How far off it is from claim `H`.** Four tests, three pass:

| | Claim `H` in the fixture | The market | Same? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Underlying | Commercial transit through the Strait of Hormuz | Arrivals of ships through the Strait of Hormuz | **Yes** |
| Deadline | 2026-11-01 | 2026-11-01 03:59 UTC | **Yes** (to the day) |
| Resolution source | "Lloyd's List transit counts." | IMF PortWatch transit calls | **No** — different counter |
| Threshold | **At least 14 consecutive days** of unrestricted transit | A **7-day moving average ≥ 60 on any one date** | **No**, and the market's test is much easier: one qualifying print settles it, where `H` needs a fortnight held |

So it is a near miss, of exactly the kind R11 anticipated: *the ending could be
rewritten to name the real contract exactly.* The rewrite is two sentences of
`resolution.criteria` and one `source`.

---

## The keyless API as it actually behaves today

Everything below was observed, not remembered. **ADR-0010's description of this
API is right in substance and wrong in three details** — see the end of this
section.

### Getting there at all

On this machine the LAN resolver answers **NXDOMAIN** for every
`polymarket.com` host while 1.1.1.1 answers normally:

```
$ nslookup gamma-api.polymarket.com
** server can't find gamma-api.polymarket.com: NXDOMAIN
$ nslookup gamma-api.polymarket.com 1.1.1.1
Name: gamma-api.polymarket.com   Address: 104.18.34.205
```

Every call below therefore carries `--resolve <host>:443:<address>`. That is a
fact about Kent's network, not about Polymarket — **but it means a live read
will fail on this machine unless the resolver is changed**, which matters for
whether the opt-in live read can be demoed here at all.

### `GET https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/public-search?q=…` — finding things

Works, keyless, HTTP 200. Returns `{"events": [...], "pagination": {"hasMore",
"totalResults"}}`. Parameters that work: `q`, `limit_per_type`,
`events_status=active`.

**Its matching is loose and it will embarrass you.** `q=brent` returns 159
results, every one of them a person called Brent or Brentford FC. `q=oil` and
`q=tanker` are excellent. Treat it as a way to find candidates by hand, never as
a way to decide a contract exists.

### `GET https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/events?slug=…` — the market record

Works, keyless. Takes repeated `slug=` parameters and returns an array of event
objects, each with a `markets[]` array. This is the one call a recorded-quote
loader needs: it carries the identifiers, the rules, the state, the size **and**
a usable bid and offer, so a quote can be taken without touching the order book
at all. The docs also offer `/events/slug/<slug>`, `/events/<id>`,
`/markets/<id>` and `/events/keyset?closed=false&after_cursor=…` for paging.

Trimmed, from `event-hormuz-oct31.json`:

```jsonc
[{ "id": "830253",
   "slug": "strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to-normal-by-october-31-20260810151043583",
   "title": "Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by October 31?",
   "active": true, "closed": false, "restricted": true,
   "liquidity": 119387.4051, "volume": 754974.3103, "openInterest": 398671.8829,
   "endDate": "2026-11-01T03:59:00Z",
   "markets": [{
     "id": "3501950",
     "question": "Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by October 31?",
     "conditionId": "0x405b56fc75f56d7635a94df9836d6cb6f9b9571d1fd33eb165c1e59d1d11801f",
     "description": "This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes …",
     "resolutionSource": "",                       // empty; the rules are in `description`
     "outcomes":       "[\"Yes\", \"No\"]",        // a STRING holding JSON
     "outcomePrices":  "[\"0.07\", \"0.93\"]",     // a STRING; rounded display, not the mid
     "clobTokenIds":   "[\"653180…541\", \"112428…453\"]",   // a STRING; index-for-index with `outcomes`
     "bestBid": 0.06, "bestAsk": 0.08, "spread": 0.02, "lastTradePrice": 0.08,
     "liquidityNum": 119187.2751, "volumeNum": 754974.3103, "volume24hr": 5061.1837,
     "active": true, "closed": false, "acceptingOrders": true, "archived": false,
     "orderPriceMinTickSize": 0.01, "orderMinSize": 5,
     "endDate": "2026-11-01T03:59:00Z", "endDateIso": "2026-11-01",
     "updatedAt": "2026-09-21T14:42:00.323164Z"   // the ROW's update time, not a quote time
   }]}]
```

**Three traps in that shape.** `outcomes`, `outcomePrices` and `clobTokenIds`
are **JSON strings that must be parsed a second time** — a generated type that
calls them arrays is wrong. `liquidity` is a string while `liquidityNum` is a
number, for the same value. And **`outcomePrices` is not the midpoint**: here it
says `0.07` while the book says 6/8, and on a settled market it snaps to `1`/`0`
while the book still reads 0.999/1.

### `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/book?token_id=…` — the order book

Works, keyless. Priced per **outcome token**, not per market.

```jsonc
{ "market": "0x405b56fc…801f",        // = the gamma conditionId
  "asset_id": "65318042…080541",      // = the outcome token id
  "timestamp": "1790002107921",       // milliseconds since epoch, AS A STRING → 14:48:27.921Z
  "hash": "ee972deb64697ea2bb2e04703702d611ceaed9ba",
  "bids": [ …, {"price":"0.05","size":"32102.28"}, {"price":"0.06","size":"6624.83"} ],
  "asks": [ …, {"price":"0.09","size":"2591.99"},  {"price":"0.08","size":"9693.3"} ],
  "min_order_size": "5", "tick_size": "0.01", "neg_risk": false,
  "last_trade_price": "0.08" }
```

**`bids` are ascending and `asks` are descending, so the best of each is the
LAST element.** Reading `bids[0]` gets the worst bid in the book — here `0.04`
instead of `0.06`, a three-point error that would look plausible. Every price
and size is a **string**.

This is the only endpoint that hands back a **timestamp for the quote itself**.
If a recorded quote is to say when it was true, it comes from here.

### `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/midpoint?token_id=…`

Works, keyless. `{"mid":"0.07"}` — a string, and **no timestamp**.

### `GET https://clob.polymarket.com/price?token_id=…&side=buy|sell`

Works, keyless. `side=buy` → `{"price":"0.06"}`, which is the **best bid**;
`side=sell` → `{"price":"0.08"}`, the **best offer**. So `side` names the side of
the book, not your intention. The documentation writes it uppercase
(`side=BUY`); lowercase worked. Getting this backwards inverts your cost of
crossing.

### Also documented, not called by me

`/spread`, `/last-trade-price`, and the POST batch forms `/books`, `/prices`,
`/midpoints`, `/spreads`, `/last-trades-prices` — one round trip for many
tokens, which is the right shape for `make record-quotes`. History lives at
`https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2/prices-history?token_id=…&interval=1d`, and
it accepts `as_of`, which is interesting for FR-30's pastcast.

### A YES/NO market's two tokens

One market, two tokens, complementary prices: `outcomes[0]` = "Yes" and
`clobTokenIds[0]` is its token. The docs' worked example is a trader buying
"No at the complementary price". Here YES mid is .07 and gamma's display prices
are `["0.07","0.93"]`. **The two books are separate books**, so 1 − NO mid need
not equal YES mid exactly; read the token you are actually quoting.

### What a closed or resolved market returns

The object is still served in full. From the September WTI event:

```jsonc
{ "id": "3866513", "question": "Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $100 in September?",
  "active": true, "closed": true, "acceptingOrders": false,
  "umaResolutionStatus": "resolved",
  "outcomePrices": "[\"1\", \"0\"]",
  "bestBid": 0.999, "bestAsk": 1, "lastTradePrice": 0.995, "spread": 0.001 }
```

Note `active` stays **true** while `closed` is true. **A loader must decide from
`closed` and `acceptingOrders`, never from the price** — the book on a settled
market reads 0.999/1, so a midpoint of .9995 would be shown as a live quote.

### Where ADR-0010 is wrong

| ADR-0010 says | What I found |
|---|---|
| *"read-only `/events` and `/markets`"* | True, and there is more: `/public-search`, `/markets/slug/…`, `/events/keyset` for paging, `/tags`, `/series`. |
| *"rate limits of roughly 4,000 requests per 10 s overall, 500 for `/events` and 300 for `/markets`"* | **I could not find this anywhere in today's documentation.** `llms.txt` lists 178 pages; the only rate-limit pages are *Builder Tiers* (order actions) and a perps page. There is no published limit for keyless market-data reads. The ADR states a number nobody can now cite — which is the same defect the FRED paragraph correctly calls out as "folklore". |
| *"A contract's mid-price … becomes `MarketBelief.p`"* | Right, and available two ways: `/midpoint`, or derived from gamma's `bestBid`/`bestAsk`. |
| *"the quoted spread becomes the range"* | **Wrong in kind.** The spread is a cost of crossing, not an uncertainty interval — see the next section. |
| *"The geographic restrictions apply to placing orders … not to reads"* | Consistent with what I saw: every read returned 200 with no geo check, and `restricted: true` sits on the market object as a trading flag. I did not test the documented `/api-reference/geoblock` endpoint. |

---

## What the `Quote` shape gets right, lacks, and gets wrong

Against `venue, contract_id, p, spread, as_of, url, source` (finance digest §2.1).

**Right.** `venue` and `url` are fine. `p` as the mid is exactly what
`/midpoint` returns. `spread` as offer-minus-bid is exactly gamma's own `spread`
field (here `0.02`, and `0.08 − 0.06`). `source: fetched | recorded | user` is
the right three-way split.

**Lacks — seven things, in the order they will bite.**

1. **`contract_id` is one field for three identifiers, and the wrong one is
   useless.** A Polymarket contract has a `conditionId` (on-chain), a numeric
   gamma market `id`, and an **outcome token id** — and only the token id buys
   you a price. Store all three.
2. **No side.** YES is .07 and NO is .93 on the same contract. `ContractPayoff`
   already carries `side`; `Quote` cannot say which token it priced.
3. **`as_of: date` throws away the time.** The book moves within the day and the
   CLOB hands back milliseconds. Store a timestamp; print the date.
4. **No `best_bid` / `best_ask`.** Store what was read and derive `p` and
   `spread` from it, not the other way round — that is the difference between a
   quote that can say why and one that asserts.
5. **No liquidity or volume.** A .07 mid over $119k of resting orders is a
   different claim from a .07 mid over an empty book. Both numbers are in the
   response.
6. **No `closed` / `accepting_orders`.** Without them a recorded quote on a
   settled market renders as live, and settled markets do **not** print 1.00.
7. **No question text, rules or end date.** The whole point of this exercise is
   that a reader can check the venue asks the same question. The `description`
   and `endDate` belong beside the number. `tick_size` (0.01) and `orderMinSize`
   (5) belong there too: **an edge smaller than one tick is not tradeable**, and
   the card should refuse to call it an edge.

**Wrong — two.**

1. **The spread must not become the range.** ADR-0010 says *"the quoted spread
   becomes the range"* and the fixture writes `market=Belief(p=0.48, lo=0.45,
   hi=0.52)` — a seven-point interval built from a two-point spread, by an
   arithmetic nobody can state. A bid-offer spread is a **transaction cost**. It
   belongs in `costs` (half of it), where the digest already puts it, and in the
   break-even. **The venue publishes no uncertainty interval at all**, so the
   honest `market` belief is a point with a cost beside it, not a range. This is
   Kent's second veto in miniature: `lo` and `hi` there trace to no input, rule
   or source.
2. **Do not take `p` from `outcomePrices`.** It is a rounded display figure:
   `0.07` where the book says 6/8, and `1`/`0` on a settled market whose book
   says 0.999/1.

---

## Terms, attribution, and what I could and could not establish

**Documented, and directly quotable** — https://docs.polymarket.com/market-data/discover-markets :

> Find the events and markets your integration needs, from a specific Polymarket
> link to a broader view of what is active. **This data is public and does not
> require authentication.**

**Rate limits: I could not find a published limit for keyless market-data
reads.** `https://docs.polymarket.com/llms.txt` lists 178 pages; the only ones
mentioning rate limits are the builder-programme tiers and a perps page, both
about **order actions**, not reads. I did not test a limit by hitting one — that
would be impolite and I made about twenty-five calls in total.

**Terms of use: not established.** `https://polymarket.com/tos` returns HTTP 200
and 260 kB, but the page is rendered in the browser and the served HTML carries
only navigation — no terms text. **I did not read Polymarket's terms of use and
cannot tell you what they say about redistributing a quote or committing a dated
quote file to a public repository.** The footer links present in the HTML are
*Privacy · Terms of Use · Market Integrity · Transparency · Docs*, and the
operating entities are named as *Adventure One QSS Inc.* and *QCX LLC d/b/a
Polymarket US, a CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Market*. **Somebody should
read the terms before a quote file is committed** — that is fifteen minutes and
it is not a thing to guess at.

**Attribution: I found no required attribution line** of the kind FRED insists
on. The absence is not permission; see the previous paragraph.

**Nothing saved carries a secret.** One run used `-D` and captured a Cloudflare
`__cf_bm` bot-management cookie; that file was deleted, not saved. Every saved
file was grepped for `set-cookie`, `__cf_bm`, `authorization`, `api_key`,
`POLY_`, `secret` and `passphrase`: the only hits are the words *authorization*
and *Army Secretary* inside market descriptions, and the *names* of builder
header fields (no values) in the documentation page.

---

## Recommendation for Kent — best first

### 1. Recommended: name the Hormuz contract, and keep the Brent ending honest about having none

Two edits to the fixture, and the demo gains a clickable venue price **and**
keeps the "no contract" path on screen — both halves of the story on one map.

**(a) Rewrite claim `H`'s resolution to the venue's own words**, so the
comparison is like with like:

> criteria: "IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls
> ('Arrivals of Ships') for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any
> date up to 31 October 2026."
> source: "IMF PortWatch transit-call data for the Strait of Hormuz."
> by: 2026-11-01 (unchanged — it already agrees with the market)

**(b) Add one `market` ending off `H`** — call it `M3` — with a
`ContractPayoff(venue="Polymarket", contract_id=<the condition id>,
title="Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by October 31?", side="yes")`,
and record its quote: **mid .07, bid .06, offer .08, read 2026-09-21 14:48 UTC.**

**(c) Leave `M1` exactly where it is**, as the `no_contract` case, printing
*"no contract quotes this claim — edge not calculable"*. With no quote there is
no break-even in probability; the honest break-even for the Brent trade is a
**price** — *"this pays if front-month Brent settles below $68"* — and it needs
the FRED `DCOILBRENTEU` spot anchor the digest already plans (§2.4), not a
Polymarket number.

**Cost:** the two fixture edits are small. The structural cost is real and worth
saying out loud: **`H` is the hypothesis, and on the branch it is supposed true**,
so `M3`'s edge must be computed from the **base** world or it is exactly the
A1 trap. The digest's `priced(base, shown, …)` signature already forces that.
**Buys:** a live, liquid, $755k contract, whose deadline matches to the day,
that a reader can open in a browser from the Inspector.

**What the card will say, and it is worth reading twice:** the model's
unconditional number for `H` is its prior, **.35**; the venue says **.07**. That
is a 28-point disagreement, and it is the single most interesting sentence this
product can print — provided the tool is honest that most of the gap is the
*claim* being harder to satisfy than it looked, not alpha. Until (a) is done,
the right label is `NotComparable(reason="different_question")`.

### 2. Alternative: add `M3` and touch nothing else

Skip (a). The venue price is still real, clickable and recorded, and the card
prints `different_question` with both questions side by side. **Cheaper, and
arguably more honest** — it demonstrates the `NotComparable` path on a real
contract instead of a missing one. **Costs** the headline "the model says X, the
venue says Y" moment, which becomes "the venue asks a different question, here
is how".

### 3. The fallback R11 names, if Kent wants no new claim at all

Keep the stand-in, mark `M1`'s quote `source: "user"` and print *"no contract
quotes this claim — edge not calculable"* with a price break-even. **This is
what happens by default and it is defensible** — but it leaves a map on which
nothing is priced, on a venue that in fact prices four of its seven claims to
within a near miss.

### 4. Regardless of 1–3: fix `N1`, and consider `S`

`N1.not_tradeable_reason` — *"No venue quotes a contract on a diplomatic
round"* — is **false**, and cheaply falsified by anyone who looks. Either rewrite
`N1` as a `market` claim naming **"US x Iran diplomatic meeting by October 31,
2026?"** (.33/.35, $184k traded, and its rules explicitly admit *"Indirect
in-person diplomacy through designated mediators"*), or rewrite the reason to
the truth: *"the contracts that exist ask about any mediated US-Iran round, not
specifically an Omani-mediated one."* The branch's `S` has the same
opportunity in the NO side of **"US x Iran ceasefire continues through October
31?"** (.51/.52) — but that market is **US-initiated strikes only**, where `S`
would accept an Israeli one, so it is a near miss to be labelled, not adopted.

---

## What I did not check

- **Polymarket's terms of use.** The page is client-rendered and I did not read
  the text. This is the one open question that bears directly on committing a
  dated quote file to a public repository.
- **The fee schedule** (`/trading/fees`). So the `costs` term in a break-even is
  half the spread only; taker fees, if any, are not in my numbers.
- **Any rate limit, by testing.** I made roughly twenty-five calls and stopped.
- **The website's own search interface in a browser.** I used
  `/public-search`, which is the endpoint the site itself calls, but I did not
  confirm that by watching the site.
- **Whether a Brent market ever existed and closed.** My unfiltered `q=brent`
  search returned ten events and all were people or Brentford; I did not page
  through all 159 results.
- **Kalshi**, which ADR-0010 names third and which is stronger on commodities —
  a Brent contract may well exist there. Not my brief; worth an hour.
- **The POST batch endpoints** (`/books`, `/midpoints`) that `make record-quotes`
  would actually want, and `data-api`'s `prices-history`. Documented, not called.
- **`/api-reference/geoblock`**, so I cannot confirm ADR-0010's claim about
  reads being ungeoblocked beyond the fact that all twenty-five of mine worked.
- **Whether an October WTI monthly event appears on 1 October.** The pattern
  suggests it will; the September one ends 2026-10-01 and no October event exists
  today. If Kent wants a *crude* contract rather than a *Hormuz* one, that is the
  thing to look at again in ten days — it would still be WTI, not Brent.

"""A belief: a likelihood with an honest range and a name on it.

A bare number on a box is a claim from nowhere. A belief is a likelihood that
says whose it is and how sure it is: a value between 0 and 1, a range around it,
and an owner — the model, the user, or a market. Every claim on the map carries
up to three of them side by side, and they are never combined into one.

That is the product in one design choice. The model's .61, the market's .48 and
your own .30 on the same claim are not three attempts at one true number to be
averaged away. They are the disagreement you are about to trade: model minus
market is the edge, user minus model is the argument you are having with the
tool.

Both classes here are frozen — once built, an instance cannot be changed. A
change is a new instance, recorded as an intervention on a branch.
"""

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator


class Belief(BaseModel):
    """A likelihood with an honest range and a name on it.

    `p` is the likelihood, `lo` and `hi` are the range around it, and `owner`
    says whose number this is. There are exactly three owners and no code path
    ever combines two of them into one number.

    A belief is a number, never text. This layer does not round it and does not
    store it as a string; rounding happens once, at the moment of display.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    # Open question 1 in spec/graph/belief.md: a belief records no provenance,
    # so a model number anchored on a documented count and one asserted from
    # nothing look alike. Owner is not yet the whole answer.
    p: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description=(
            "How likely the claim is to come out true, from 0 (certainly not) to 1 (certainly yes)."
        ),
    )
    lo: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description="The bottom of the honest range around `p`. Never above `p`.",
    )
    hi: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description="The top of the honest range around `p`. Never below `p`.",
    )
    owner: Literal["model", "user", "market"] = Field(
        description=(
            "Whose number this is: the model's estimate, the user's own, or a live "
            "price at a venue."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _range_is_ordered(self) -> "Belief":
        """Check that low is at most the likelihood, which is at most high.

        The field bounds above already cover 0 and 1; this covers the order.

        Returns:
            This same belief, once the order has been checked.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the three numbers are not in order.
        """
        if not (self.lo <= self.p <= self.hi):
            raise ValueError(
                "a belief must satisfy low <= likelihood <= high; got "
                f"low={self.lo}, likelihood={self.p}, high={self.hi}"
            )
        return self


class Beliefs(BaseModel):
    """The three voices on one claim: the model's, the user's, and a market's.

    Three named slots, deliberately not a dictionary, so that nothing can loop
    over them and average them by accident. `model` is always present. `user` is
    absent until the user says what they think. `market` is absent when no venue
    quotes this claim — and absent means the words "no market", never a blank and
    never a stand-in number.

    The field named `model` is legal. Pydantic protects names beginning with
    `model_`, so `model_config` and `model_dump` are reserved; plain `model` is
    not one of them. It stays `model` because that is the word the shared
    vocabulary uses, on the canvas and in the code alike.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    model: Belief = Field(
        description=(
            "What the model thinks, with this claim's causes taken into account. Always present."
        ),
    )
    user: Belief | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "What the user thinks. Written only by the `believe` intervention. None means "
            "the user has not said."
        ),
    )
    market: Belief | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "What a venue is currently pricing, read live and read-only. None means no "
            "venue quotes this claim."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _owners_match_slots(self) -> "Beliefs":
        """Check that each slot holds a belief owned by the voice the slot is named for.

        A belief sitting in the wrong slot would make the never-merge rule
        unenforceable: a user's number could sit in the model's chip and nothing
        would notice.

        Returns:
            This same set of beliefs, once every slot has been checked.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If any slot holds a belief owned by someone else.
        """
        for slot, belief in (("model", self.model), ("user", self.user), ("market", self.market)):
            if belief is not None and belief.owner != slot:
                raise ValueError(f"the '{slot}' slot holds a belief owned by '{belief.owner}'")
        return self

30	model proposal could plausibly break comes back as a violation carrying a plain

trade** — a contract at a venue, or an instrument and which way you would take
it. It never names what that costs. Prices, spreads and the moment a quote was
read belong to the layer that fetches them, and they reach the map as the
market's own likelihood on the claim, which carries its own owner and can say
where it came from.

Some rules about a proposition are checked here, when the object is built, and
some are checked later over the whole map. The line between them: a rule only our
own code could break raises an exception at construction; a rule a well-formed
model proposal could plausibly break comes back as a violation carrying a plain
sentence the user reads. That is why a `market` claim with no payoff can be built

class Resolution(BaseModel):
    """How a claim gets settled: the test, who applies it, and by when.

    Every proposition has one. A claim with no resolution is a vibe, and a
    likelihood attached to a vibe can never be scored, right or wrong.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    criteria: str = Field(
        description=(
            "The test, written so that two people reading it would agree on the "
            "answer. A counted threshold over a named window, not a mood: "
            "'at least 14 consecutive days of X', not 'things return to normal'."
        )
    )
    source: str = Field(
        description=(
            "Who or what applies the test: a named publication, exchange, agency "
            "or venue — the one that actually publishes this number, not 'the news'."
        )
    )
    by: date = Field(
        description=(
            "The date by which the test has been applied. After this date the "
            "claim is true or false — never still open."
        )
    )


class BaseRate(BaseModel):
    """How often this kind of thing has happened before: k times out of n.

    The outside view — the anchor a likelihood starts from before anything
    specific to this case is considered. Optional, because some claims have no
    honest reference class, and absent is better than invented.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    reference_class: str = Field(
        description=(
            "The set of past cases being counted, stated precisely enough that "
            "someone else could count them again: what kind of case, over what "
            "period, and what made a case count."
        )
    )
    k: int = Field(ge=0, description="How many cases in that set came out true.")
    n: int = Field(gt=0, description="How many cases are in that set altogether.")
    # Open question 3 in spec/graph/proposition.md: these are plain web addresses
    # while a link's citations are a `Source` record with a title and a date. If
    # `Source` stays, does this field adopt it?
    sources: tuple[str, ...] = Field(
        default=(),
        description=(
            "Web addresses where the count can be checked. Empty means the count "
            "is the model's own recollection, and nothing downstream of it may "
            "claim to be documented."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _k_within_n(self) -> "BaseRate":
        """Check that the count of true cases is not larger than the set it is drawn from.

        You cannot count 7 cases out of 5.

        Returns:
            This same base rate, once the two counts have been checked.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If k is larger than n.
        """
        if self.k > self.n:
            raise ValueError(
                f"a base rate counts {self.k} cases out of {self.n}; k must not exceed n"
            )
        return self


class Evidence(BaseModel):
    """One published item that supports or undercuts a claim.

    Evidence moves no number by itself in this version. It is what the Inspector —
    the persistent side panel beside the canvas — shows when the user asks why a
    likelihood is what it is, and it is what lets the panel say "two for, one
    against" without re-reading the sources.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    claim: str = Field(description="What the source says, in one sentence, in our words.")
    # Open question 3 in spec/graph/proposition.md: a plain web address here,
    # while a link's citations carry a title and a date fetched as well.
    url: str = Field(description="Where to read it, so the reader can check us.")
    direction: Literal[1, -1] = Field(
        description=(
            "1 if this supports the proposition, -1 if it cuts against it. There "
            "is no 0: an item that points neither way is not attached at all."
        )
    )
    weight: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description=(
            "How much this item counts, from 0 (barely) to 1 (decisive). Elicited "
            "and unitless; shown as a bar, never as a decimal."
        ),
    )


class ContractPayoff(BaseModel):
    """A named contract at a named venue, and which side of it you would take.

    The kind of ending where somebody already sells exactly this claim: a
    prediction-market contract that settles on the same question the claim asks.
    Nothing here says what the contract costs, because that is a live price rather
    than a fact about the map.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    kind: Literal["contract"] = "contract"
    venue: str = Field(
        description="Where the contract trades, by the venue's own name: 'Polymarket', 'Kalshi'."
    )
    contract_id: str = Field(
        description=(
            "How that venue identifies this exact contract, so a reader can look it up and "
            "a later step can fetch its price."

    )
    title: str = Field(
        description=(
            "The contract's question in the venue's own words, so a person reading the map "
            "can see it is really the same question the claim asks."
        )
    )
    side: Literal["yes", "no"] = Field(
        description=(
            "'yes' if you make money when the claim comes true, 'no' if you make money when "
            "it fails."
        )
    )


class PricePayoff(BaseModel):
    """An instrument you would buy or sell, which way, and how far you expect it to move.

    The kind of ending where no contract asks this question, but something traded
    moves when the answer changes: a futures contract, a ticker, one fund against
    another.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    kind: Literal["price"] = "price"
    instrument: str = Field(
        description=(
            "The thing you would buy or sell, named the way its venue names it: a ticker, "
            "a futures contract, one fund against another."
        )
    )
    direction: Literal["long", "short"] = Field(
        description=(
            "'long' if the position makes money when the claim comes true, "
            "'short' if it makes money when the claim fails."
        )
    )
    move: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        description=(
            "How far the instrument's price is expected to move if the claim comes out true, "
            "as a fraction of that price: 0.03 means three per cent. The side is carried by "
            "`direction`, so this number is never negative."
        ),
    )


Payoff = Annotated[ContractPayoff | PricePayoff, Field(discriminator="kind")]
"""What a `market` terminal is worth: a named contract, or a move in a price.

Read the `kind` field to know which of the two it is. Two shapes rather than one
because the two endings are genuinely different: one names a question somebody
already sells, the other names something traded that moves when the answer
changes. Squeezing both into one shape left every field meaning two things.
"""


class Proposition(BaseModel):
    """A claim that will be true or false by a date, judged by a named source.

    The unit the whole map is built from. Never a vibe ("tensions ease"); always
    a check ("at least 14 consecutive days of unrestricted commercial transit
    through the Strait of Hormuz per Lloyd's List, by 2026-11-01").

    Frozen. A proposition is never edited in place; a change to one is an
    intervention recorded on a branch.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    id: PropositionId = Field(
        description=(
            "This proposition's identifier, minted by our code before the proposition is built."
        )
    )
    claim: str = Field(
        description=(
            "The claim in one sentence, as a person would say it out loud. The "
            "precise, settleable version lives in `resolution.criteria`."
        )
    )
    kind: Literal["hypothesis", "event", "market", "not_tradeable"] = Field(
        description=(
            "What this proposition is for: `hypothesis` is the user's root input, "
            "`event` a step in the middle, `market` an ending that names an "
            "instrument, `not_tradeable` an ending that names why there is none."
        )
    )
    resolution: Resolution = Field(description="How and when this claim gets settled, and by whom.")
    prior: Belief = Field(
        description=(
            "The model's likelihood for this claim before its causes are taken "
            "into account. Always owned by `model`."
        )
    )
    beliefs: Beliefs = Field(
        description=(
            "The three likelihoods shown side by side: the model's (causes taken "
            "into account), the user's, and the market's. Never merged."
        )
    )
    base_rate: BaseRate | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "How often this kind of thing has happened before, when there is an "
            "honest reference class. None means there is not one."
        ),
    )
    evidence: tuple[Evidence, ...] = Field(
        default=(),
        description=(
            "Published items for and against, each with a direction and a weight. "
            "Empty is honest; invented sources are not."
        ),
    )
    payoff: Payoff | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "What you would trade. Required when `kind` is `market` — required by "
            "the map's validity rules, not by this class."
        ),
    )
    not_tradeable_reason: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Why this chain ends without an instrument, in one plain sentence. "
            "Required when `kind` is `not_tradeable` — again by the validity rules."
        ),
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _prior_is_the_models(self) -> "Proposition":
        """Check that the prior is the model's own number.

        The engine builds this belief, so any other owner is a bug in our own
        code rather than something a model proposal could do to us.

        Returns:
            This same proposition, once the prior's owner has been checked.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the prior is owned by anyone but the model.
        """
        if self.prior.owner != "model":
            raise ValueError(

            )

334	    """Each version's answer for each claim, one row per version and one column per day."""
335	
336	    inner_spread: Mapping[PropositionId, Numbers]
337	    """How much the worlds inside each version disagreed, per version and per day.
338	
339	    What the noise correction needs. With this and the likelihoods above, a reader
340	    can rebuild any day's band exactly as the world reports it — which is how a
341	    difference between two worlds gets each world's band on whichever day it wants
342	    to read the change on, without a world carrying millions of numbers itself.
343	    """
344	
345	    def counting_for(self, claim_id: PropositionId) -> Numbers:
346	        """Say how much each version counts when this claim's own number is read.
347	
348	        **The one rule, named once here because everything that reads a number or
349	        its direction has to obey the same one.** Every version counts the same,
350	        unless what was observed is evidence about this claim — the claims in
351	        `reweighted` — and then each version counts by the share of its worlds that
352	        survived **the observations that are evidence about this claim**, and no
353	        others. The likelihood, the band, the width a change list reports on
354	        another day and the direction of a move are all read with the vector this
355	        gives back, so none of them can be counted one way and another of them
356	        another way.
357	
358	        **And a world that kept nothing at all counts every version the same
359	        again.** Nothing survived what was observed anywhere, so there is no
360	        surviving share to weigh anything by; counting evenly at least reports the
361	        map rather than dividing by nothing, and the world carries a loud warning
362	        saying the reader is looking at the map rather than at an answer. That
363	        fallback lives here and nowhere else, so every reader gets it.
364	
365	        Args:
366	            claim_id: The claim whose number is being read.
367	
368	        Returns:
369	            How much each version counts, one number per version. Never all
370	            zeroes, so anything dividing by its total is safe.
371	        """
372	        counting = self.weights[claim_id]
373	        evenly: Numbers = numpy.ones_like(counting)
374	        if claim_id not in self.reweighted:
375	            return evenly
376	        return counting if counting.sum() > 0.0 else evenly

379	def propagate(
380	    graph: Graph,
381	    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...],
382	    *,
383	    as_of: date,
384	    seed: int,
385	    versions: int = 2_000,
386	    worlds: int = 8,
387	    introduced_by: Mapping[LinkId, int] = NOTHING_ADDED,
388	) -> World:
389	    """Work every likelihood on a map through time, and say how sure we are of each.
390	
391	    Pure: no clock, no network, no global random state. The same map, values and
392	    seed give a byte-identical world on any machine, which is what makes a
393	    three-day-old screenshot reproducible from three values.
394	
395	    The map must already be one the validity rules accept. In particular it must
396	    have no loops once feedback arrows are set aside, because the claims have to
397	    be worked through causes-before-effects and a map that runs round in circles
398	    has no such order.
399	
400	    Args:
401	        graph: The map a fold left behind. Never changed.
402	        assignments: Every value that fold fixed, in the order the edits were made.
403	            When a claim has more than one, the last is the one in force and the
404	            earlier ones stay for the record.
405	        as_of: Day zero — the day the window starts on. This layer reads no clock,
406	            so the day is always passed in.
407	        seed: The one number every random draw comes from.
408	        versions: The outer loop — how many versions of the map to try. Each one is
409	            a coherent set of numbers this model would have stood behind.
410	        worlds: The inner loop — how many worlds to run under each version. At
411	            least two, or there is no inner spread to subtract.
412	        introduced_by: Which edit added each arrow, by position in the branch, so a
413	            supposition something undermined can name the edit responsible. Leaving
414	            it out is only safe when no supposition can be undermined; when one is,
415	            and its arrow is not in here, that is a broken promise between our own
416	            two pieces of code and it is said out loud rather than guessed at.
417	
418	    Returns:
419	        One world: a likelihood and a range for every claim on the day it is
420	        judged, a likelihood and a named state for every day the series is drawn
421	        at — every day of the window until the window outruns the cap, and then
422	        the days `series_days` names — every supposition that was undermined, and
423	        a sentence for anything the reader should be told.
424	
425	    Raises:
426	        ValueError: If a supposition was undermined by an arrow that `introduced_by`
427	            does not account for. The one thing this file raises for, and why is in
428	            `_retractions`.
429	    """
430	    setup = _prepare(graph, assignments, as_of)
431	    sample = _draw(setup, seed=seed, versions=versions, worlds=worlds)
432	    return _world_from(
433	        graph,
434	        assignments,
435	        setup,
436	        sample,
437	        _retractions(setup, introduced_by),
438	        seed=seed,
439	        versions=versions,
440	        worlds=worlds,
441	    )

448	    exact, so this recomputes the same 2 000 versions the world was built from

487	def _sent_days(setup: "_Setup") -> NDArray[numpy.int64]:
488	    """Where the days a reader is given sit among the days worked out.
489	
490	    The days worked out are the days sent plus the handful the arithmetic must land
491	    on exactly, so every sent day is among them and this is a lookup rather than a

498	def _versions_from(setup: "_Setup", sample: "_Sample") -> Versions:
499	    """Gather the version-by-version numbers a run produced into one record.
500	
501	    Written once and used twice: by `versions_of`, which recomputes a world's
502	    versions for a comparison, and by the step that turns a run into a world,
503	    which needs the same record to ask how much each version counts. Two copies of
504	    this would be two chances for a world and the difference between two worlds to
505	    disagree about what a version is.
506	
507	    Args:
508	        setup: Everything chance had no say in.
509	        sample: What the two loops produced.
510	
511	    Returns:
512	        One record of the version-by-version numbers.
513	    """
514	    # Thinned to the days a reader is given, so that a difference between two
515	    # worlds compares exactly the days the two of them show and nothing else.
516	    sent = _sent_days(setup)
517	    return Versions(
518	        days=tuple(int(setup.points[one]) for one in sent),
519	        weights=sample.weights,
520	        reweighted=frozenset().union(*setup.observation_reach.values())
521	        if setup.observation_reach
522	        else frozenset(),
523	        priors=sample.priors,
524	        likelihood={one: row[:, sent] for one, row in sample.likelihood.items()},
525	        inner_spread={one: row[:, sent] for one, row in sample.inner_spread.items()},
526	    )

554	@dataclass(frozen=True)
555	class _Setup:
556	    """The whole of a world that does not depend on chance: who causes whom, and when."""
557	
558	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition]
559	    order: tuple[PropositionId, ...]
560	    arrows_into: Mapping[PropositionId, tuple[Link, ...]]
561	    spells: Mapping[PropositionId, tuple[_Spell, ...]]
562	    settled: Mapping[PropositionId, int]
563	    day_zero: date
564	    days: int
565	    points: NDArray[numpy.int64]
566	    sent: NDArray[numpy.int64]
567	    read_at: Mapping[PropositionId, int]
568	    shape_rows: Mapping[LinkId, Numbers]

573	
574	def _prepare(
575	    graph: Graph,
576	    assignments: tuple[Assignment, ...],
577	    as_of: date,
578	    every_day: bool = False,
579	) -> _Setup:
580	    """Work out everything about a world that chance has no say in.
581	
582	    The window, the order claims are worked through in, the day each claim's clock
583	    starts, which stretch of days each fixed value holds over, which suppositions
584	    something undermined and on which day, and what the reader should be warned
585	    about. All of it is the same in every one of the sixteen thousand draws, which
586	    is exactly why it is computed once.
587	
588	    Args:
589	        graph: The map a fold left behind.
590	        assignments: Every value that fold fixed, in order.
591	        as_of: Day zero.
592	        every_day: Work every day of the window out rather than the days a
593	            reader is sent plus the ones the arithmetic must land on exactly.
594	            Nothing that ships passes this; `_versions_on_every_day` does, so that
595	            working out fewer days can be checked against working out all of them.
596	
597	    Returns:
598	        Everything the draw below needs and nothing that depends on a seed.
599	    """
600	    claims = {one.id: one for one in graph.propositions}
601	    ordinary = _ordinary_arrows(graph, claims)
602	    order = _causes_before_effects(claims, ordinary)
603	    arrows_into: dict[PropositionId, tuple[Link, ...]] = {
604	        claim_id: tuple(one for one in ordinary if one.target == claim_id) for claim_id in claims
605	    }
606	
607	    fixed_on: dict[PropositionId, list[Assignment]] = {claim_id: [] for claim_id in claims}
608	    for one in assignments:
609	        if one.target in fixed_on:
610	            fixed_on[one.target].append(one)
611	    settled = _settled_days(order, arrows_into, fixed_on, as_of)
612	
613	    days = _window_length(graph, as_of)
614	    spells = {
615	        claim_id: _spells_on(fixed_on[claim_id], arrows_into[claim_id], settled, as_of)
616	        for claim_id in claims
617	    }
618	
619	    # **The days the numbers are worked out on.** Two kinds, and the difference is
620	    # the whole of what makes an edit local.
621	    #
622	    # The days a reader is *sent* — at most 180 of them, evenly spaced, with every
623	    # claim's resolve-by day always among them. These move when the window's length
624	    # moves, and that is allowed: they decide where a line is *drawn*, nothing more.
625	    #
626	    # And the days the arithmetic must land on **exactly**: the day each claim's
627	    # clock starts, because a one-off push fires then, and the day each observation
628	    # speaks, because that is when worlds are thrown away. Reading either off the
629	    # nearest drawn day is what used to let the window's length re-time a push, so
630	    # that an inserted claim at one end of a map moved a claim at the other by
631	    # `.096`. They are put on the grid instead, and every lookup is then exact.
632	    #
633	    # Adding them cannot move anything, and that is why this is safe rather than
634	    # merely cheaper: a claim's answer on a given day is a function of that day and
635	    # of the map's own timings, never of which *other* days happen to be worked
636	    # out. So the grid decides only where the series is evaluated.
637	    sent = (
638	        numpy.arange(days + 1, dtype=numpy.int64)
639	        if every_day
640	        else _days_to_send(claims, as_of, days)
641	    )
642	    must_be_exact = {min(max(0, one), days) for one in settled.values()}
643	    # An observation carries no date today — `Observe` has no `at`, so it always
644	    # speaks on day zero, which is already on the grid as the first sent day. This
645	    # term is therefore dead, and it is written anyway: the day an observation
646	    # speaks is a day the arithmetic reads by name, and the moment `Observe` grows
647	    # a date the grid must already be landing on it. Adding it later, after the
648	    # field existed, would be a defect waiting to be found twice.
649	    for stretches in spells.values():
650	        must_be_exact |= {
651	            min(max(0, one.starts), days) for one in stretches if one.kind == "observe"
652	        }
653	    points = numpy.union1d(sent, numpy.array(sorted(must_be_exact), dtype=numpy.int64))
654	    read_at = {
655	        claim_id: _point_of(points, _day_index(one.resolution.by, as_of, days))
656	        for claim_id, one in claims.items()
657	    }
658	
659	    shape_rows = {one.id: _shape_row(one, settled[one.source], points) for one in ordinary}
660	
661	    return _Setup(
662	        claims=claims,
663	        order=order,
664	        arrows_into=arrows_into,
665	        spells=spells,
666	        settled=settled,
667	        day_zero=as_of,
668	        days=days,
669	        points=points,
670	        sent=sent,
671	        read_at=read_at,
672	        shape_rows=shape_rows,
673	        observation_reach=_observation_reach(claims, ordinary, spells),
674	        states=_states(claims, spells, shape_rows, points),
675	        warnings=_warnings_about(graph, claims, days),
676	    )

679	def _ordinary_arrows(graph: Graph, claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition]) -> tuple[Link, ...]:
680	    """List the arrows the arithmetic actually uses, **in the order the map carries them**.
681	
682	    A feedback arrow — a market changing the world it is measuring — is left out:
683	    it is carried as data in this version and worked through by a later stack, the
684	    same way the map's own loop check leaves it out. An arrow with an end that is
685	    not on the map is left out too; it already has its own complaint.
686	
687	    The order is the map's own, and that order means something: folding a branch
688	    appends each `insert`'s arrows after the ones already there, so an arrow's
689	    place on the map is the order it arrived in. That is both a settled order to
690	    add the pushes on a claim up in — so two runs agree to the last digit — and
691	    the tie-break when two arrows undermine a supposition on the very same day.
692	
693	    Args:
694	        graph: The map to read.
695	        claims: Every claim on it, by identifier.
696	
697	    Returns:
698	        The ordinary arrows, in the order the map carries them.
699	    """
700	    return tuple(
701	        one
702	        for one in graph.links
703	        if not one.reflexive and one.source in claims and one.target in claims
704	    )
705	
706	
707	def _causes_before_effects(
708	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition], arrows: Sequence[Link]
709	) -> tuple[PropositionId, ...]:
710	    """Put the claims in an order that always works out a cause before its effects.
711	
712	    Ties — claims that no arrow orders relative to one another — are broken by
713	    identifier, so the order depends on the map and never on the order the claims
714	    happen to be written down in.
715	
716	    Args:
717	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
718	        arrows: The ordinary arrows.
719	
720	    Returns:
721	        Every claim's identifier, causes first.
722	
723	    Raises:
724	        networkx.NetworkXUnfeasible: If the map runs round in circles once feedback
725	            arrows are set aside. Such a map has no causes-before-effects order at
726	            all, and the validity rules refuse it long before it reaches here.
727	    """
728	    walkable: networkx.DiGraph[PropositionId] = networkx.DiGraph()
729	    walkable.add_nodes_from(sorted(claims))
730	    walkable.add_edges_from((one.source, one.target) for one in arrows)
731	    return tuple(networkx.lexicographical_topological_sort(walkable))

734	def _day_index(when: date | None, day_zero: date, cap: int | None = None) -> int:
735	    """Turn a date into a whole number of days after day zero.
736	
737	    Nothing before day zero: a value fixed from a day already gone holds from the
738	    beginning of the window.
739	
740	    Args:
741	        when: The date, or nothing at all, which means day zero.
742	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
743	        cap: The last day of the window, when the answer must sit inside it.
744	
745	    Returns:
746	        The day's number, counting from zero.
747	    """
748	    if when is None:
749	        return 0
750	    index = max(0, (when - day_zero).days)
751	    return index if cap is None else min(index, cap)

754	def _window_length(graph: Graph, day_zero: date) -> int:
755	    """Say how many days the window runs for: day zero to the last day anything is judged."""
756	    return max(_day_index(one.resolution.by, day_zero) for one in graph.propositions)

758	
759	def _days_to_send(
760	    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition], day_zero: date, days: int
761	) -> NDArray[numpy.int64]:
762	    """Choose which days of the window a claim's series carries to the reader.
763	
764	    **A cap on the evenly spaced points alone**, and never a decision about timing.
765	    Ordinarily every day of the window. Past 180 days that is more points than
766	    anybody scrubs through, so a series is drawn at 180 evenly spaced days instead
767	    — **and every claim's own resolve-by day is kept whatever the cap says**, so a
768	    map judged on more than 180 different days sends one point per judged day,
769	    which is more than the cap and is the honest answer. That is not a nicety: a
770	    tile's headline number is read on the claim's own resolve-by day, and if that
771	    day were not on the claim's own series the number on the tile would not be a
772	    point of the line drawn beneath it.
773	
774	    These days are not, by themselves, the days the engine works out: `_prepare`
775	    adds to them every day the arithmetic must land on exactly. So the cap does
776	    bound the work — the days worked out are these plus that handful — but it is
777	    never what decides when a push fires.
778	
779	    It was once the whole grid the engine worked on, and that was a defect. A push
780	    fires on the day its cause is settled, read off the days worked out — so
781	    thinning them made that day depend on how long the window was, and an edit at
782	    one end of a map could re-time a claim at the other end that nothing connected
783	    it to. Measured before it was separated: an inserted claim that stretched a
784	    window from 31 days to 365 moved a claim in a wholly separate piece of the map
785	    by `.096`.
786	
787	    Args:
788	        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
789	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
790	        days: How long the window is.
791	
792	    Returns:
793	        The days to send, in order.
794	    """
795	    judged = numpy.array(
796	        sorted({_day_index(one.resolution.by, day_zero, days) for one in claims.values()}),
797	        dtype=numpy.int64,
798	    )
799	    if days + 1 <= SERIES_CAP:
800	        return numpy.arange(days + 1, dtype=numpy.int64)
801	    spare = max(2, SERIES_CAP - len(judged))
802	    evenly = numpy.rint(numpy.linspace(0, days, spare)).astype(numpy.int64)
803	    return numpy.union1d(judged, evenly).astype(numpy.int64)
804	
805	
806	def _settled_days(
807	    order: Sequence[PropositionId],
808	    arrows_into: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[Link]],
809	    fixed_on: Mapping[PropositionId, Sequence[Assignment]],
810	    day_zero: date,
811	) -> dict[PropositionId, int]:
812	    """Say which day each claim's clock starts on — the day it is *settled*.
813	
814	    Three rules, in order. If an edit fixed the claim's value, its clock starts on
815	    the earliest day any of them holds from. Otherwise it starts on the earliest
816	    day a live incoming arrow reaches it: the day that arrow's cause was settled,
817	    plus the arrow's delay, rounded up to a whole day. A claim with neither is
818	    settled on day zero, because the map carries no timing information about it at
819	    all.
820	
821	    **Being settled is not being true.** A claim with nothing fixing it is sampled
822	    from its own prior in every draw; its clock starting says only when the arrows
823	    leaving it begin to measure their delays from. Conflating the two is the
824	    mistake this paragraph exists to prevent.
825	
826	    Args:
827	        order: Every claim, causes first.
828	        arrows_into: The ordinary arrows pointing at each claim.
829	        fixed_on: Every value fixed on each claim, in the order the edits were made.
830	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
831	
832	    Returns:
833	        The day each claim's clock starts on.
834	    """
835	    settled: dict[PropositionId, int] = {}
836	    for claim_id in order:
837	        fixed = fixed_on[claim_id]
838	        if fixed:
839	            settled[claim_id] = min(_day_index(one.at, day_zero) for one in fixed)
840	            continue
841	        arrivals = [math.ceil(settled[one.source] + one.lag) for one in arrows_into[claim_id]]
842	        settled[claim_id] = min(arrivals) if arrivals else 0
843	    return settled

846	def _shape_row(link: Link, settled: int, points: NDArray[numpy.int64]) -> Numbers:
847	    """Work out how big one arrow's push is on each day, as a fraction of its full size.
848	
849	    A plain function of elapsed days, and zero before the cause was settled. A
850	    **spike** is nothing through the delay, then full size, halving every half-life
851	    afterwards. A **step** is nothing through the delay, then full size, held. A
852	    **ramp** climbs from nothing to full size across the delay, then holds.
853	
854	    A ramp with no delay at all needs no special case: the days at or past the
855	    delay are settled first, which for a delay of nothing is every day from the
856	    cause onwards, and the climb is then left with no days to climb over. Such a
857	    ramp behaves as a step, as a consequence of the shape rather than as a rule.
858	
859	    A spike always says how fast it fades — a spike that does not is a fault in the
860	    map, refused by its own rules before it ever reaches here. The line below is
861	    the net under a map that arrived some other way, and it holds the push rather
862	    than dividing by nothing.
863	
864	    Args:
865	        link: The arrow.
866	        settled: The day the arrow's cause was settled.
867	        points: The days to work out.
868	
869	    Returns:
870	        One number per day, between 0 and 1.
871	    """
872	    elapsed = points.astype(numpy.float64) - settled
873	    landed = elapsed >= link.lag
874	    row = numpy.zeros_like(elapsed)
875	    row[landed] = 1.0
876	    if link.shape == "step":
877	        return row
878	    if link.shape == "ramp":
879	        climbing = (elapsed >= 0.0) & ~landed
880	        row[climbing] = elapsed[climbing] / link.lag
881	        return row
882	    if link.half_life is None or link.half_life <= 0.0:
883	        return row
884	    row[landed] = 2.0 ** (-(elapsed[landed] - link.lag) / link.half_life)
885	    return row

888	def _opposing(arrows: Sequence[Link], supposed: bool) -> list[Link]:
889	    """List the arrows pushing against a supposed value, in the order they were given.

892	    supposed **false** when its push is positive. An arrow of no strength pushes
893	    neither way and opposes nothing.

898	def _spells_on(
899	    fixed: Sequence[Assignment],
900	    arrows: Sequence[Link],
901	    settled: Mapping[PropositionId, int],
902	    day_zero: date,
903	) -> tuple[_Spell, ...]:
904	    """Work out which stretch of days each edit's word holds over, on one claim.
905	
906	    Each edit's word holds from its own day until the next edit on the same claim
907	    has something to say, because a later assignment overrides an earlier one. A
908	    supposition also stops early, on the day the **cause** of the first arrow
909	    pushing against it was settled — not the day that arrow's push reaches full
910	    size, because tying the end of a supposition to the arrival would tie "do I
911	    still take your word for this" to a delay parameter.
912	
913	    A user may suppose a claim again after it was undermined. The second
914	    supposition holds from its own day until something undermines it again, and the
915	    series then reads supposed, withdrawn, pushed, supposed — which falls straight
916	    out of "a later assignment overrides an earlier one" rather than needing a rule
917	    of its own.
918	
919	    When two arrows undermine a supposition on the very same day, the one that
920	    arrived on the map first wins. That is the arrow's own place on the map, which
921	    is the order the edits added them in: the base map's arrows, then each `insert`'s
922	    arrows in the order it listed them. Some settled answer is needed or the badge
923	    would name a different arrow on different runs and a world would stop replaying.
924	
925	    Args:
926	        fixed: Every value fixed on this claim, in the order the edits were made.
927	        arrows: The ordinary arrows pointing at it, in the order the map carries them.
928	        settled: The day each claim's clock starts on.
929	        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
930	
931	    Returns:
932	        One stretch per edit, in the order the edits were made.
933	    """
934	    where = {one.id: index for index, one in enumerate(arrows)}
935	    days = [_day_index(one.at, day_zero) for one in fixed]
936	    spells: list[_Spell] = []
937	    for index, one in enumerate(fixed):
938	        starts = days[index]
939	        ends = days[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(days) else None
940	        undermined_on, undermined_by = None, None
941	        if one.kind == "do":
942	            against = [
943	                (max(starts, settled[arrow.source]), where[arrow.id], arrow)
944	                for arrow in _opposing(arrows, one.value)
945	            ]
946	            live = [entry for entry in against if ends is None or entry[0] < ends]
947	            if live:
948	                undermined_on, _, undermined_by = min(live, key=lambda entry: entry[:2])
949	        spells.append(
950	            _Spell(
951	                kind=one.kind,
952	                value=one.value,
953	                starts=starts,
954	                ends=ends,
955	                undermined_on=undermined_on,
956	                undermined_by=undermined_by,
957	            )
958	        )
959	    return tuple(spells)

962	def _retractions(setup: _Setup, introduced_by: Mapping[LinkId, int]) -> tuple[Retraction, ...]:
963	    """Write down every supposition something undermined, and which edit is to blame.
964	
965	    **Which edit added the undermining arrow is always known**, and that is a
966	    theorem rather than a convention: supposing a claim cuts every arrow pointing
967	    at it at that moment, so any arrow that later pushes against it was added
968	    afterwards, by an edit with a position in the branch.
969	
970	    Args:
971	        setup: Everything chance has no say in.
972	        introduced_by: Which edit added each arrow, by position in the branch.
973	
974	    Returns:
975	        One retraction per supposition that ended, claim by claim.
976	
977	    Raises:
978	        ValueError: If an arrow that undermined a supposition is not in the list of
979	            which edit added what. That is the one thing this file raises for, and
980	            it is a broken promise between our own two pieces of code rather than
981	            anything a user did: whoever asked for this world folded a branch onto
982	            the map and then did not say which edit added which arrow.
983	    """
984	    found: list[Retraction] = []
985	    for claim_id in sorted(setup.spells):
986	        for spell in setup.spells[claim_id]:
987	            if spell.undermined_on is None or spell.undermined_by is None:
988	                continue
989	            arrow = spell.undermined_by
990	            if arrow.id not in introduced_by:
991	                raise ValueError(
992	                    "A supposition was undermined by an arrow that nothing says was added "
993	                    "by an edit. Every arrow that can undermine a supposition was added "
994	                    "after it, so the branch's edits have to be passed in alongside the "
995	                    "values they fixed."
996	                )
997	            found.append(
998	                Retraction(
999	                    target=claim_id,
1000	                    at=setup.day_zero + timedelta(days=spell.undermined_on),
1001	                    by_link=arrow.id,
1002	                    by_claim=arrow.source,
1003	                    by=introduced_by[arrow.id],
1004	                )
